title: College Football model recap — 2026-09-04
summary: The model went 9/11 (82%) on graded College Football picks.
body: Matchday's model graded 11 College Football picks this stretch, hitting on 9 of them (82%). Over the same 10 games with a market line, the betting market favorite hit 90% of the time.

On calibration: picks stated at 70-80% hit 100% of the time (3 games); picks stated at 80-90% hit 67% of the time (3 games); picks stated at 90+% hit 100% of the time (4 games). A well-calibrated model's stated confidence should roughly match its actual hit rate in each band.
The strongest signal lately has been talent or squad quality: when it favored a side, that side won 90% of the time (10 games).

Among this week's College Football storylines: the biggest upset was Colorado winning 13-14 against Georgia Tech (the market gave that result only about 32%); the model's best call was Utah in Utah vs Idaho at 92% confidence; its biggest miss was picking Rutgers in Rutgers vs Massachusetts, but Massachusetts won instead.

This is Matchday's own model reporting on itself for anyone to use. Every pick is locked before kickoff and graded automatically once the game finishes; none are rewritten after the fact. See the Q&A page for how the model works.

title: Transparent Weekly Scorecard - August 9-15, 2026
summary: 26 hits, 20 misses, one unresolved grade, and incomplete MLB ledger coverage.

highlights.best_call: Tampa Bay Rays over Oakland Athletics (73%)
highlights.largest_miss: Boston Red Sox over Oakland Athletics (72%)

body: The completed August 9-15 window has 47 verified MLB locks and 46 final grades: 26 hits and 20 misses. The one ungraded Cubs-Cardinals lock is excluded rather than backfilled or counted as a loss.

All 46 settled rows retain same-time regulation market snapshots. The model's Brier/log loss was 0.488/0.682 against the market's 0.494/0.687, but the model uses market context, so this narrow one-week comparison is not an independent edge claim.

Only 15 locks and 14 grades reached the append-only MLB ledger. Frozen official pick receipts support the score, while incomplete ledger reconciliation, no August 15 lock, and the unresolved grade remain explicit integrity limitations.

title: What We’re Refining Before We Count More Results
summary: How Matchday is tightening prediction locks, grading, calibration reporting, and MLB eligibility.
body: We are refining the proof around every reported prediction: pregame locks, like-for-like outcomes, market comparisons, and uncertainty metrics.
MLB is back in active coverage, but older rows without pregame lock evidence remain excluded from the official score.
The standard stays stable: no legacy mixing, no rewritten picks, and no improvement claim from accuracy alone.
